source.title: Polysemantic Attention Head in a 4-Layer Transformer

record.file_problem: None; the full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests the causal importance of an induction-pattern head on constructed prompts by BOS-ablating its attention pattern. This is a conceptual test, not a reproduction of induction-head formation during training.
record.gate_note: The post also reports BOS-ablation results for bigger-indentation and fuzzy-previous-token behaviours. Those do not test the claim versions about induction heads, phase change, or few-shot task learning, so they are not included as rows. Figure 1 is referenced, but its numerical distribution is not stated in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: On constructed copying prompts in a small attention-only model (attn-only-4l), the post causally tests whether head 1.4's induction-style attention matters for predicting the repeated continuation. It does this by BOS-ablating the head's attention at the induction position. This bears only on the 'implements [A][B]…[A]→[B]' part of V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that head 1.4 exhibits multiple simple attention patterns (induction, fuzzy previous-token, bigger indentation), each relevant to performance. They also say labelling heads by a single narrow-task behaviour can mislead. They add that the model likely reuses one head to save parameters, and that they did not work out the mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses constructed code-like prompts and target-position BOS ablation to assess a head's contribution; it does not reproduce the original training-time formation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Ablating the induction-task target position has a much larger effect than ablating other positions.

fits_no_version.finding: The same layer-1 head acts as an induction head in some contexts and as a fuzzy previous-token head or bigger-indentation head in others. Each behaviour is causally important on its own prompt set (100%→80% and 100%→4% top-1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heads labelled as induction heads are often polysemantic, performing other functions such as previous-token attention in other contexts. Labelling a head by one narrow-task behaviour can mislead.

record.problems: The evidence is from one 4-layer attention-only model and constructed prompt sets; the post reports no uncertainty estimates. It tests the head's contribution on the induction task, not its proposed composition mechanism or formation during training.
record.rows_left_out: No numerical Figure 1 classification values are available in the supplied text, so none are recorded. The bigger-indentation and previous-token ablation results are outside the claim versions.

untested.parts: Composition with an earlier (layer-0) previous-token head. How or when the head forms. Whether the head's output copies the attended token (no OV analysis).

missing.what: Share of training-distribution attention patterns classified as previous+induction for head 1.4 (Figure 1). The numbers are not given in the text.

record.verdict_notes: A single 4-layer attention-only model, constructed prompts, no uncertainty reported. The post's main contribution is polysemanticity rather than a test of induction-head theory, so its support for V1 is narrow.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests the importance of head 1.4 on an induction prompt task, but does not test composition with an earlier previous-token head or how the head forms.
Not tested; the study does not assess most in-context learning or large transformers.
Not tested across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
Not tested; no comparison of training data or setups for induction formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Not tested; the constructed next-token prediction tasks are not an assessment of few-shot task learning.
Not tested; the study does not examine transitions during training.

rows.measure: Percentage of examples where the correct next token is the top-predicted token
rows.note: The post reports the clean and corrupted-run values for the 120-prompt dataset.
rows.check: The ablation replaces the head's whole attention row at that destination with a BOS-only pattern. It removes whatever the head does there, not only its induction attention. The text does not state clearly whether the green target is the copied token.

relationships.condition: attn-only-4l, head 1.4, 120 constructed code-like induction prompts
relationships.reason: BOS-ablating the head at the induction position cuts top-1 accuracy from 93% to 25% and probability from 0.28 to 0.09. Other positions drop <5 pp (r1-r4). The mechanism by composition is not tested.
relationships.display_finding: BOS ablation of head 1.4 at the induction position reduced top-1 accuracy from 93% to 25% and probability from 0.28 to 0.09, while other positions lost under 5 percentage points; composition was untested.
